newsitem.title: USA: Grandmother released from US jail but must pay tax.
newsitem.headline: Grandmother released from US jail but must pay tax.

text.p: A judge on Tuesday agreed to release a 60-year-old grandmother who spent six weeks in jail claiming she gave away a $250,000 inheritance to the needy and could not pay $40,000 in estate taxes and fees.

A lawyer for Hortencia Bohen, who has been jailed since May 20 for contempt of court, was told she must make a good-faith effort to raise the money from friends and family or she would be sent back to the Lake County jail in northwest Indiana.

Bohen was the sole beneficiary of steelworker Thomas Villenueva in 1995 but she said she gave the $250,000 inheritance to the homeless and has no documentation of her charity. She initially misidentified herself as Villenueva's niece, which reduced her estate tax bill by about $7,000, but later acknowledged being his "longtime friend." The remaining $33,000 she owes represents legal, accounting and other administrative expenses related to the estate.

"See, I told you. I ain't got nothin'," a shackled Bohen told the judge, County Probate Commissioner Joseph Skozen, on Friday when participants in the case watched the opening of an empty bank safe deposit box she had rented. Attorneys for her creditors suspect she may have hidden the funds.

"After she got locked up I figured we'd hear from her in an hour; certainly the next day at the latest," said Joseph Costanza, a lawyer for a bank involved in the case. "But you just can't talk to her. She is, to put it mildly, a very determined woman."
